method.closed_system: Slider-crank cylinder volume and 1-zone ideal-gas first-law update, conservative midpoint pressure work; heat-release interval follows normalized Wiebe law.
method.two_stroke: One 360-degree ported cycle. EPC-trapped charge is compressed/combusted/expanded to EPO; estimated exhaust blowdown, transfer-pressure interval and exhaust tail close the gas-exchange path; crankcase scavenge pump loss remains separate.
method.four_stroke: One 720-degree true four-stroke cycle. IVC-trapped charge is compressed/combusted/expanded to EVO; separate exhaust/intake valve-open boundary-pressure path closes the cycle; open-system mass/enthalpy exchange is not solved.
method.energy_state: Cycle-resolved kinetic energy uses d(0.5*J_eff(theta)*omega^2)/d(theta)=net torque; J_eff adds the profile's estimated equivalent piston mass times slider-crank (dy/dtheta)^2 to the aircraft configuration's installed rotor inertia. Prop load is reevaluated at instantaneous angular speed and integrated with a midpoint energy update. Rod angular kinetic energy and connecting-rod distribution are omitted.
method.combustion_waveform_during_speed_ripple: A full pressure/torque waveform is generated at each candidate mean RPM, then held fixed over that one-cycle energy map. Instantaneous propeller and table-based mechanical/pump/valve losses vary with RPM; charge, fuel, and combustion do not adapt within the cycle. This is a conditional averaging-error experiment, not a transient engine model.
method.propeller_load: Independent reproduction of current 12-annulus, uniform-chord installed-prop surrogate, followed by the ideal actuator-disk lower-bound refusal for positive static thrust.
method.phase_alias_probe: Coarse uniform-angle midpoint sampling of a 0.0625-degree reference pressure-torque waveform, with 16 grid-phase offsets; linear interpolation only supplies sample values. This reports numerical alias sensitivity for an inferred waveform and is not a measurement or runtime fixed-dt test.
method.fixed_carrier: The carrier is held at zero axial speed. This isolates an installed prop/engine pair and is not free-flight behavior.

primary_method_references.use: Crank-angle-resolved single-zone combustion formulation; engine-specific measured calibration is not imported.

primary_method_references.use: Supports treating two-stroke port exchange and scavenging as distinct from the closed compression/expansion segment; its multi-zone flow method is more detailed than this reduced estimate.

primary_method_references.title: Simulation of a Crankcase Scavenged, Two-Stroke, SI Engine and Comparisons with Experimental Data
primary_method_references.use: Coupled crankcase/cylinder/inlet control-volume precedent; highlights what this single-zone port-boundary oracle omits.

primary_method_references.title: O.S. MAX-55AX manufacturer specifications
primary_method_references.use: Bore, stroke, displacement and engine identity for the 2T candidate.

primary_method_references.title: O.S. FS-64V manufacturer specifications
primary_method_references.use: Bore, stroke, displacement and engine identity for the 4T candidate.

primary_method_references.title: Development And Analysis of a Group 1 UAV Series Hybrid Power System with Two Engine Options (AIAA 2016-5011)
primary_method_references.use: Table 1 gives Omega 10% fuel properties for the same blend tested with O.S. MAX-55AX (2-cycle) and O.S. FS 56-a (4-cycle). The paper's engine-output data are not imported as calibration targets here; FS 56-a is not FS-64V.

limitations: Neither manufacturer publishes these candidates' compression ratio, connecting-rod ratio, port/valve timing, in-cylinder pressure trace, heat-transfer history, residual fraction or engine rotating inertia.

Open-system scavenging/intake/exhaust boundary pressures are imposed estimates; mass exchange, short-circuit fuel loss, crankcase dynamics, exhaust resonance, variable properties, wall heat transfer and glow ignition kinetics are not solved.

AIAA-2016-5011 reports O.S. MAX-55AX 2-cycle and O.S. FS 56-a 4-cycle engine results using the Omega 10% blend. Its Table 1 fuel properties are borrowed; its engine-output results are not imported as calibration targets in this pressure oracle, and FS 56-a is not FS-64V.

The profile root and pressure-oracle root use different candidate closures. Only the within-oracle angle-mean versus periodic-map comparison tests the mean reduction numerically for the declared waveform; no result proves actual engine accuracy.
The annular propeller method preserves estimated uniform chord/section coefficients. Its dynamic evaluation and ideal-power lower bound do not constitute a measured propeller map or aircraft data.

provenance.engine_displacement_bore_stroke: O.S. manufacturer dimensions from the linked product page; displacement checked against bore×stroke.
provenance.compression_ratio_rod_ratio_port_valve_e: Not published for these candidate engines; explicit engineering assumptions and ranges below.
provenance.fuel_formula: Candidate profile fuel properties use AIAA-2016-5011 Table 1 for Omega 10% (72% methanol, 10% nitromethane, 18% castor oil by volume), the same blend tested with O.S. MAX-55AX 2-cycle and O.S. FS 56-a 4-cycle engines. Fuel properties alone are borrowed; the paper's engine-output results are not used as calibration targets, and FS 56-a is not FS-64V.
provenance.combustion_law: Normalized single-Wiebe prescribed mass-burn fraction, used as an assumed heat-release shape; not inferred from measured cylinder pressure.
provenance.profile_comparison: The source candidate kernel computes cycle work as burned fuel × LHV × a generated indicated-efficiency table. The pressure oracle instead integrates a crank-angle first-law pressure-volume path; disagreement compares two inferred closures, not measurement error.
provenance.dynamic_comparison: The periodic crank-energy map uses the independent pressure trace plus exact installed candidate prop parameters and RPM-varying annular load. It is a fixed-carrier software experiment; no in-flight, prop-map or physical-engine validation is implied.

nominal_assumptions.open_flow_shape: linear blowdown; sin^2 scavenge-pressure pulse; ambient tail

rpm_constraint_check.interpretation: A rating point above the installed propeller limit is retained as a manufacturer engine reference point, not a valid installed operating prediction.

rated_point.sensitivity_interpretation: Unweighted one-factor scenario endpoints; not a confidence interval or physical bound.

mean_root_comparisons.assumption: Full admission, static 0 m/s carrier, 1.225 kg/m^3; restoring roots only.
mean_root_comparisons.inertia_sensitivity_method: Primary periodic orbit uses the aircraft configuration's installed rotating_inertia value. Sensitivity cases use 0.5× and 2× that estimate; rotating mass distribution and crank contribution are not measured. The profile's separate estimated equivalent piston mass is included as angle-dependent inertia, with one-cycle 1%-to-5%-of-dry-mass perturbations around the primary speed (not re-solved equilibria).
mean_root_comparisons.averaging_error_scope: At each declared inferred pressure/flow/timing/inertia hypothesis, compare the angle-averaged pressure-work balance to the periodic crank-energy solution using the same pressure-work cycle and installed prop load. The profile-root difference additionally includes different inferred engine work/loss closures; neither comparison establishes empirical accuracy.

quadrature_and_anti_alias_audit.interpretation: The event-aligned sweep tests crank-angle quadrature resolution. The separate phase sweep intentionally does not align coarse uniform samples to events and quantifies phase-sensitive midpoint integration error for the fine prescribed waveform. This does not prove that a runtime physics step aliases a real engine waveform.

status.independent_thermodynamic_convergence: evaluated by step refinement; see sweep
status.mean_reduction_comparison: computed for the stated inferred hypotheses only
